fuzzy_measure_pairing — MEASURE1D caliper op

• Data kinds: image2d × measurehandle → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.fuzzy_measure_pairing(image, measure, sigma=1.0, threshold=0.1, pair_size=None) (to call the implementation directly, import measuring1d; measuring1d.fuzzy_measure_pairing(image, measure, sigma=1.0, threshold=0.1, pair_size=None); from the registry, opsmeasure1d.get("fuzzy_measure_pairing"))

Usage

Selects the edge pair that best matches a fuzzy criterion (expected width pair_size) (fuzzy_measure_pairing).

Procedure: measure_pairs(image, measure, sigma, threshold) takes pairs of adjacent edges of opposite polarity, attaches fuzzy_score = exp(-((width - pair_size) / (0.5 pair_size))^2) to each pair, and sorts them in descending score order. Exactly the expected width gives 1; a width off by ±0.5 pair_size gives e^-1 ≈ 0.37. The first element is the best-matching pair.

• image: 2-D float (grey values in the input's units).

• measure: dict from gen_measure_rectangle2 / gen_measure_arc.

• sigma: smoothing σ of the profile [samples]. threshold: minimum |grey difference| of edges to accept (image units).

• pair_size: expected width [px]. With None, no sorting and no scoring; the result of measure_pairs (in order along the measuring line) is returned as is. 0 and negative values are not validated (with 0 the denominator becomes 1e-9 and the scores of all pairs collapse to nearly 0 or 1).

• Returns: list of pair dicts (type table). Each dict has first / second (sample index), width [px], first_point / second_point ((row, col)), first_amplitude / second_amplitude, fuzzy_score. If there is not even 1 pair, an empty list (no exception).

To cut by a lower/upper bound on the width, filter this result by width yourself (this op only ranks; it does not exclude by a threshold).
